policy.missing_evidence: Unknown is distinct from experimentally absent.
policy.negative_evidence: Keep nonbinding, absent coordinate contacts, and mutation-with-no-effect distinct; never infer one from another.
policy.transfer: Search shared receptor and related interface, then verify species, construct, sequence identities, substitutions, chain mapping, and geometry. Shared receptor alone does not validate a transferred contact.

hatta2000.review_scope: Primary abstract read; Wiley full text/PDF routes returned abstract. Exact construct methods not verified.
hatta2000.findings: Soluble receptor alanine scan used SPR against BMP4; thioredoxin fusion was cleaved after bacterial expression. I52A/F75A caused approximately 17/15-fold weaker affinity; E54A/T62A/T64A about 3/4/4-fold. Y70A did not reduce affinity. Representative-mutant CD did not reveal folding changes.
hatta2000.numbering_caveat: All six reported residue identities fit mouse BMPR1A at paper position+33. Human has A97 where mouse has T97 (paper T64). Species/construct inference is not full-method confirmation.
hatta2000.allowed_inference: Contributing receptor surface; atom partners and exact BMP4 geometry are not measured.

khodr2021.review_scope: Primary full text methods/results and Table2 read
khodr2021.assay_context: Immobilized dimeric receptor-Fc, BLI, 1:1 kinetic fitting; BMP4 produced in E.coli; avidity and construct dependence limit transfer to monomeric ECD affinities.
khodr2021.glycan_context: Separate ALK3 comparison reported nonglycosylated BMP4 KD1.32+/-0.48 versus glycosylated0.30+/-0.06 nM. Protein-only sampling is a defined approximation.
khodr2021.allowed_inference: Supports receptor compatibility, not a six-chain structure or residue contact accuracy.

weber2007.review_scope: Primary full text read from Europe PMC XML snapshot
weber2007.findings: 2H62 contains BMP2 dimer plus one receptor of each class. The paper reports hexamer in solution and crystal packing blocking remaining sites. W60/Y42 are ACVR2B binding determinants for BMP2; L61 backbone-N/S88-Ogamma is a geometric contact with little WT energetic contribution. BMPR1A contacts both ligand chains.
weber2007.allowed_inference: Mapped BMP2 interface hypothesis. Do not label its RMSD/DockQ as BMP4 accuracy.

protein_interface_rules_v1.title: Protein–protein interface inspection rules
protein_interface_rules_v1.purpose: Agent instructions for inspecting interfaces and proposing guidance terms. These are heuristic checks, not a calibrated binding-affinity predictor or an executable scoring function.
protein_interface_rules_v1.core_instruction: Evaluate atom-level chemistry and three-dimensional geometry. Use general physical plausibility to filter models, and experimentally supported interface constraints to supply target specificity.
preparation: Identify exact sequences, constructs, chain copies and biological assembly. Map all paper residue numbers to the modeled sequences before activating constraints.
Resolve alternate conformations and document missing residues or atoms. Preserve an original coordinate file and record any preparation or refinement.
Assign protonation consistently with the assay context, add hydrogens where required, and record glycan, water, disulfide and terminal-group assumptions.
Record software versions and classifier thresholds. Do not mix different contact definitions across runs.

rules.name: Hydrogen bonding
rules.look_for: Chemically valid donor and acceptor atoms with appropriate distances and directional geometry.
rules.action: Classify atom pairs using an established hydrogen-bond detector; retain measured distances and angles.
rules.caution: A short residue-to-residue distance or an angle-free polar-contact label does not establish a hydrogen bond.

rules.name: Electrostatics
rules.look_for: Complementary charged groups, protonation-dependent contacts and nearby charge networks.
rules.action: Inspect charge placement together with solvent exposure and desolvation using a consistent energy model.
rules.caution: An opposite-charge residue pair is a candidate interaction, not an unconditional reward; its environment changes its contribution.

rules.name: Nonpolar packing
rules.look_for: Burial of complementary nonpolar surfaces with favorable van der Waals packing.
rules.action: Measure interface burial and inspect packing; report separately for each ligand–receptor interface.
rules.caution: Increasing contact count or buried area alone does not establish favorable binding energy.

rules.name: Steric compatibility
rules.look_for: Excessive overlap, strained backbone geometry and implausible side-chain conformations.
rules.action: Use MolProbity/PROBE for all-atom clashes and geometry validation.
rules.caution: PROBE serious clashes use non-hydrogen-bond overlaps greater than 0.4 Å with explicit hydrogens. A custom heavy-atom distance count is a different metric.

rules.name: Aromatic interactions
rules.look_for: Aromatic ring arrangements and cation–π contacts.
rules.action: Use plane-aware classification, not only a residue-distance cutoff.
rules.caution: Two nearby aromatic residues do not automatically form a favorable π interaction.

rules.name: Polar satisfaction
rules.look_for: Polar or charged groups buried without suitable partners.
rules.action: Flag candidate unsatisfied groups and assess their hydrogen-bond and solvation context.
rules.caution: Missing water or uncertain protonation can change the interpretation.

rules.name: Structural integrity
rules.look_for: Backbone, rotamer, bond-geometry or disulfide strain introduced while satisfying interface constraints.
rules.action: Inspect local validation outliers as well as the interface score.
rules.caution: A model should not distort its individual protein folds to satisfy a contact reward.

rules.name: Energetic hotspots
rules.look_for: Mutation or binding-energy evidence that a residue contributes substantially to affinity.
rules.action: Track experimentally supported hotspots separately from observed structural contacts and predicted important residues.
rules.caution: A visible contact, hydrogen bond or large buried side chain is not by itself a demonstrated energetic hotspot.

evidence_labels.label: experimental_contact
evidence_labels.meaning: Contact supported by an experimental structure of this interface.

evidence_labels.label: experimental_energetic_effect
evidence_labels.meaning: Binding or mutation measurement; document whether folding or expression changes were controlled.

evidence_labels.label: transferred_hypothesis
evidence_labels.meaning: Mapped from a related ligand/receptor interface; not validated for this exact pair.

evidence_labels.label: predicted_contact
evidence_labels.meaning: Observed in a generated model; does not independently validate that model.

evidence_labels.label: generic_chemistry
evidence_labels.meaning: Physical plausibility criterion without target-specific binding evidence.

suggested_workflow: Read target-specific structural and biochemical papers first.
Map sequences and record contact evidence separately from mutation effects.
Preserve validated interface modules; add hypotheses for the unknown interfaces.
Use smooth, bounded guidance terms and penalize geometry failures. Choose weights through validation rather than assigning universal energies to contact classes.
Compare baseline and guided ensembles with matched compute and inputs; report each receptor interface and the whole assembly.
Use held-out references or experimental constraints where possible. Promote predictions to transferable hypotheses, not experimental facts.

bmp_example.contact: ActRIIB L61 backbone amide and BMP2 S88 side-chain oxygen form a central hydrogen bond in the reported structures.
bmp_example.energy_evidence: The paper describes this hydrogen bond as energetically silent for wild-type BMP2; surrounding mutations can activate its energetic contribution.
bmp_example.agent_instruction: For the reported 2.93 Å contact in your model, identify the exact atoms and check hydrogen-bond geometry before assigning the label. Use the paper's residue numbering only after sequence mapping.
bmp_example.terminology: Describe the interface as contacts between β-sheet surfaces unless actual interchain backbone hydrogen-bond patterns support a more specific description.

guardrails: Use classifier-specific definitions; do not hard-code one distance for every interaction.
Avoid double-counting one atom pair across overlapping contact classes.
Keep per-interface results so that one good receptor does not hide another poor one.
Do not infer Kd, calibrated binding probability or experimental correctness from a contact count or model energy alone.
Do not enforce a universal receptor arrangement, glycan dependency or covalent link across unrelated complexes.

arpeggio.name: PDBe Arpeggio
arpeggio.role: Rule-based interaction classification; mmCIF input and JSON output.

rosetta.name: Alford et al. 2017: Rosetta all-atom energy function
rosetta.role: Combined energetic treatment of packing, electrostatics, hydrogen bonding, solvation and conformation.

hotspots.name: Bogan and Thorn 1998: Anatomy of hot spots in protein interfaces
hotspots.role: Experimental mutation analysis separating contact area from energetic importance.

bmp2_actriib.name: Weber et al. 2007: A silent H-bond can be mutationally activated
bmp2_actriib.role: Target-specific example of geometry versus energetic contribution.

protein_interface_rules_v1.scope: Generic inspection and candidate scoring heuristics, not target-specific experimental evidence or an executable/calibrated affinity score. The BMP example supplements the existing target record.
protein_interface_rules_v1.evidence_label_scope: Vocabulary for future observations; no existing evidence_class is reclassified by this import. R8 instructs evaluation of energetic evidence; it does not establish a hotspot for any target.
